newsitem.title: INDIA: India's ONGC 1996/97 crude output seen falling.
newsitem.headline: India's ONGC 1996/97 crude output seen falling.

text.p: Crude oil production by India's Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC) in 1996/97 (April-March) is expected to drop to 29.2 million tonnes from 31.9 million the previous year, its chairman said on Thursday.
"We expect ONGC's crude production to hover around 29.2 million tonnes in 1996/97," Bikash C. Bora told a meeting of the Forum of Financial Writers in remarks made available to Reuters on Thursday.
Bora said he expected production in 1997/98 would remain at the same level.
ONGC, one of the world's top 25 oil companies, had earlier projected 1996/97 output at 31.09 million tonnes. The company produced 31.9 million tonnes of crude in 1995/96.
Bora said the production fall would be due to the need to shut some of ONGC's oilfields for rehabilitation purposes, which might take one or two years.
One company official told Reuters ONGC was encountering very complex reservior behaviour in some of the wells in Bombay High and some other fields.
The company was closing down some of the wells for better reservoir management, he said.
